description: Mitigations for explosion hazards. Prevention (eliminating explosive atmosphere) and protection (blast-resistant design, suppression) are the two strategies. DSEAR/ATEX framework.

mitigations.name: inerting
mitigations.description: Replace oxygen with inert gas to keep atmosphere below LOC (limiting oxygen concentration). Prevents explosive atmosphere forming. Common in chemical/pharma vessels.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.03. Failure: inerting system failure, O2 analyser fault, vessel opened without purging, insufficient flow rate.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: If O2 is below LOC, combustion cannot occur. Very high effectiveness when maintained. Note: creates breathing hazard — see confined space mitigations.

mitigations.name: blast_resistant_design
mitigations.description: Control rooms and occupied buildings designed to withstand blast overpressure. API 752/753 building siting studies. The structure absorbs the blast — inherent to the design.
mitigations.pfd_source: Design mitigation — can't be defeated. PFD reflects blast exceeding design rating.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Blast-resistant buildings protect occupants from overpressure up to design limit. Texas City (2005): portable buildings in blast zone killed 15 — reinforced control room survived.

mitigations.name: explosion_suppression
mitigations.description: Detects incipient explosion (pressure rise) and discharges suppressant (sodium bicarbonate, water) within milliseconds. NFPA 69. Prevents explosion from developing.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.05. Failure: detector fouled, suppressant bottle not charged, system not reset after previous activation, explosion too fast for suppression.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: When detection and discharge are fast enough, explosion is quenched before peak overpressure. Most effective for dust explosions in vessels (contained volume).

mitigations.name: explosion_venting
mitigations.description: Explosion vent panels (NFPA 68) that open at low pressure, directing blast away from occupied areas. Passive — no activation needed. Limits peak overpressure inside the vessel/room.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.03. Passive device. Failure: vent blocked/painted over, vent area insufficient for explosion severity, vent directs blast toward occupied area.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Limits internal overpressure by venting to safe area. Does not prevent the explosion — directs it. Personnel in the vent discharge zone are at risk.

mitigations.name: gas_detection
mitigations.description: Fixed gas detectors (catalytic/IR) or dust monitors with alarm at %LEL threshold. Early warning to evacuate and eliminate ignition sources before explosive atmosphere is reached.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.07. Failure: detector poisoned/fouled, wrong detection technology for the gas, insufficient coverage, alarm ignored.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Early warning enables evacuation before ignition. Does not prevent the explosion if ignition occurs before evacuation. Effectiveness is time between detection and ignition.

mitigations.name: atex_zoning
mitigations.description: DSEAR/ATEX hazardous area classification with zone-appropriate equipment (Ex-rated) and hot work controls. Administrative framework ensuring ignition sources are controlled.
mitigations.pfd_source: LOPA: PFD 0.10 for administrative controls. Failure: incorrect zone classification, non-Ex equipment brought into zone, hot work permit not obtained.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Removes ignition sources from explosive atmospheres. Effectiveness is indirect — the atmosphere may still form, but without ignition the explosion doesn't occur.
